concepts.name: Health informatics
concepts.definition: An interdisciplinary field that connects health sciences, information sciences, and management sciences and is concerned with acquiring, managing, representing, and transforming health data.

concepts.name: Purpose of health informatics
concepts.definition: Turning health data into useful knowledge that can support healthcare decisions, interventions, and processes.

concepts.name: Health information technology
concepts.definition: The digital tools and systems used in healthcare, including electronic health records, laboratory systems, patient portals, and mobile-health applications.

concepts.name: Health data science
concepts.definition: An area focused on transforming health data into knowledge that can support decisions, using methods such as statistics, computing, analytical models, machine learning, and visualization.

concepts.name: Health-data life cycle
concepts.definition: The movement of health data through connected stages: create or collect; store and protect; manage and standardize; analyze and interpret; communicate and use; and retain or dispose.

concepts.name: Structured data
concepts.definition: Data that follow a defined format and are usually stored in specific fields.

concepts.name: Unstructured data
concepts.definition: Data that do not follow a simple fixed field structure.

concepts.name: Semantic gap
concepts.definition: A situation in which recorded data and the intended clinical meaning do not match clearly.

concepts.name: Metadata
concepts.definition: Information about data, such as source, date, unit, and method.

concepts.name: Data governance
concepts.definition: The management of data together with ethical, legal, and organizational responsibility.

concepts.name: Health sciences
concepts.definition: A disciplinary contribution involving knowledge of patients, clinical care, health systems, terminology, healthcare standards, workflows, and health outcomes.

concepts.name: Information sciences
concepts.definition: A disciplinary contribution involving computing, databases, information retrieval, privacy, security, and human-computer interaction.

concepts.name: Management sciences
concepts.definition: A disciplinary contribution involving project management, quality improvement, finance, workflow, and organizational change.

concepts.name: Create or collect data
concepts.definition: The life-cycle stage in which data are produced during care, administration, monitoring, research, or patient activities.

concepts.name: Store and protect data
concepts.definition: The life-cycle stage in which data are stored in records, databases, repositories, or connected information systems while accuracy, availability, confidentiality, and appropriate access are protected.

concepts.name: Manage and standardize data
concepts.definition: The life-cycle stage in which data are checked, cleaned, organized, coded, standardized, and prepared for use.

concepts.name: Analyze and interpret data
concepts.definition: The life-cycle stage in which data are examined for summaries, comparisons, trends, relationships, and patterns and interpreted within clinical and organizational context.

concepts.name: Communicate and use information
concepts.definition: The life-cycle stage in which findings are presented to intended users and connected with decisions, process changes, policies, interventions, or research questions.

concepts.name: Retain or dispose of data
concepts.definition: The life-cycle stage in which data are kept when required and securely disposed of when no longer needed, according to policy.

concepts.name: DIKW framework
concepts.definition: A framework consisting of data, information, knowledge, and wisdom that explains how raw observations can be transformed into meaningful and useful understanding.

concepts.name: Data
concepts.definition: Discrete, unorganized, raw, and objective facts recorded from observations or transactions.

concepts.name: Information
concepts.definition: Data that have been organized, structured, and placed in context.

concepts.name: Knowledge
concepts.definition: Connected information in which relationships are understood and patterns are recognized.

concepts.name: Wisdom
concepts.definition: The appropriate application of knowledge to solve a problem or choose an action.

concepts.name: Data literacy
concepts.definition: The ability to read, understand, work with, and communicate about data.

concepts.name: Data acumen
concepts.definition: The ability to make good judgments about using data to support evidence-based decisions.

concepts.name: Core competencies in health informatics
concepts.definition: Competencies involving healthcare systems and workflows; data management; privacy, security, legal compliance, ethics, and governance; project management and quality improvement; communication and visualization; and collaboration across clinical, technical, administrative, research, and patient perspectives.

concepts.name: Data quality
concepts.definition: The condition of data as assessed through whether important values are missing, incorrect, delayed, or inconsistent.

concepts.name: Context
concepts.definition: Information about a data value that helps establish who, what, when, where, and how it represents something.

concepts.name: Data acumen foundations
concepts.definition: Basic statistics, computing, and understanding of evidence as areas of data acumen.

concepts.name: Data management
concepts.definition: Database design, storage, retrieval, and organization as an area of data acumen.

concepts.name: Data preparation
concepts.definition: Cleaning and transforming data for analysis.

concepts.name: Analysis
concepts.definition: Analytical modeling, machine learning, and interpretation as an area of data acumen.

concepts.name: Practice
concepts.definition: Healthcare workflow, reproducibility, communication, visualization, governance, and ethics as areas of data acumen.

concepts.name: Electronic health record
concepts.definition: A digital record of health information used across time and healthcare services that brings together clinical and administrative information needed to support care.

concepts.name: EHR purpose
concepts.definition: Supporting individual patient care and wider organizational activities through the entry, retrieval, review, updating, and sharing of authorized clinical and administrative information.

concepts.name: EHR contents
concepts.definition: Information that may include identification and demographics, problems, diagnoses, allergies, medications, immunizations, health history, notes, care plans, orders, results, procedures, discharge information, appointments, insurance, claims, payments, messages, education, reminders, and information from connected systems.

concepts.name: Historical development of EHR systems
concepts.definition: The movement from separate departmental electronic functions toward broader electronic patient records, connected organizational information, and wider exchange across healthcare services.

concepts.name: Interoperability
concepts.definition: The ability of different systems to connect, exchange information, and use it in a coordinated way so that the information supports appropriate action.

concepts.name: Inpatient EHR
concepts.definition: An EHR that supports care during hospital admission and across hospital departments.

concepts.name: Ambulatory EHR
concepts.definition: An EHR that supports outpatient visits before, during, and after the encounter.

concepts.name: Long-term-care EHR
concepts.definition: An EHR that supports continuing care, minimum data requirements, and communication with hospitals.

concepts.name: Personal health record
concepts.definition: A record that, along with patient portals, gives patients access to selected information and services.

concepts.name: Clinical functions
concepts.definition: Functions that directly support assessment, diagnosis, treatment, monitoring, and communication about care.

concepts.name: Administrative functions
concepts.definition: Functions that support scheduling, authorization, claims, payment, inventory, and organizational operations.

concepts.name: Primary use of EHR data
concepts.definition: Using information directly to provide and coordinate care for a patient.

concepts.name: Secondary use of EHR data
concepts.definition: Using information for another legitimate purpose beyond the immediate encounter, such as quality improvement, population health, billing, research, education, or planning.

concepts.name: Clinical documentation
concepts.definition: The recording of assessments, observations, diagnoses, interventions, and outcomes to create a shared account of what happened and why decisions were made.

concepts.name: Structured fields and templates
concepts.definition: Organized entry formats that can improve consistency but may not capture every clinical detail.

concepts.name: Free text
concepts.definition: Textual documentation that can add context but may be harder to search and analyze.

concepts.name: Orders and results workflow
concepts.definition: The movement of an authorized order to the responsible department, completion of the service, and return of the result to the EHR for review, interpretation, and follow-up.

concepts.name: Medication management and e-prescribing
concepts.definition: Electronic processes that move medication orders to pharmacy systems and may check allergies, duplicate therapy, dose, interactions, and other safety rules.

concepts.name: Clinical decision support
concepts.definition: EHR-based checks, alerts, reminders, registries, templates, and related functions that support safety, prevention, chronic-care monitoring, and follow-up.

concepts.name: Population-health tools
concepts.definition: Tools that summarize information across groups rather than one patient at a time.

concepts.name: Clinical information system
concepts.definition: A system that supports a particular area of patient care or clinical work.

concepts.name: Laboratory information system
concepts.definition: A system that supports laboratory orders, patient and test identification, specimen collection, tracking, testing, verification, reporting, and transmission of verified results to the EHR.

concepts.name: Radiology information system
concepts.definition: A system that supports imaging orders, scheduling, workflow, and reports.

concepts.name: Picture archiving and communication system
concepts.definition: A system that stores and displays medical images.

concepts.name: Pharmacy information system
concepts.definition: A system that receives medication orders and supports pharmacist review, preparation, medication information, dispensing, and exchange with the EHR and related systems.

concepts.name: System integration
concepts.definition: The connection of the EHR with specialized systems so that orders, results, status, patient identity, and other information remain consistent.

concepts.name: Shared record
concepts.definition: An integrated record in which the EHR provides a central access point while specialized systems perform detailed departmental work.

concepts.name: Patient care
concepts.definition: Care supported by assessment, diagnosis, treatment, monitoring, communication, prevention, chronic-care support, and follow-up.

concepts.name: Computerized provider order entry
concepts.definition: Electronic entry of orders by authorized providers, with orders transmitted directly to pharmacy, laboratory, radiology, or other departments.

concepts.name: Medication safety through CPOE
concepts.definition: The use of electronic medication ordering, pharmacy review, dispensing, administration, patient identification, and system checks to reduce preventable errors and improve consistency.

concepts.name: Inpatient EHR adoption stages
concepts.definition: A gradual development process that may progress from technical infrastructure and reliable electronic data to documentation, medication functions, CPOE, safety capabilities, and connections with patients and external organizations.

concepts.name: Pre-visit ambulatory workflow
concepts.definition: Activities before an outpatient visit, including scheduling, checking insurance and authorization information, updating patient information, and reviewing previous problems, tests, and planned follow-up.

concepts.name: During-visit ambulatory workflow
concepts.definition: Activities during an outpatient visit, including documentation, assessment, diagnosis, care planning, ordering tests or medications, referrals or procedures, e-prescribing, and decision-support reminders.

concepts.name: Post-visit ambulatory workflow
concepts.definition: Activities after an outpatient visit, including providing instructions, interpreting results, sending reminders and educational content, secure messaging, scheduling follow-up, and preserving the longitudinal record.

concepts.name: Tethered personal health record
concepts.definition: A personal health record connected to an organization's EHR that shares data or functions with it.

concepts.name: Untethered personal health record
concepts.definition: A stand-alone personal health record managed separately from a provider's EHR.

concepts.name: Patient portal
concepts.definition: A secure patient-facing connection to an organization's EHR that provides access to selected health information and services.

concepts.name: Proxy access
concepts.definition: Access that allows another person to manage an individual's personal health record with authorization or consent.

concepts.name: Five rights of decision support
concepts.definition: Providing the right information to the right person in the right format through the right channel at the right time.

concepts.name: Preventive-care reminder
concepts.definition: A system reminder that compares patient information with rules for screening, vaccination, or chronic-care monitoring and may display what is due, the due date, and the most recent completion date.

concepts.name: Alert fatigue
concepts.definition: A condition in which poorly designed or repeated low-value alerts interrupt workflow and may cause users to ignore useful warnings.

concepts.name: Connected patient journey
concepts.definition: A sequence linking patient scheduling and information updates, clinical documentation and orders, exchanges with laboratory and pharmacy systems, decision support, follow-up communication, and longer-term continuity and review.

concepts.name: Health information exchange
concepts.definition: The electronic sharing of health information between authorized participants.

concepts.name: Health information organization
concepts.definition: An entity that facilitates or manages health information exchange and may establish participation rules, identity processes, privacy protections, and technical services.

concepts.name: Continuity of care
concepts.definition: The availability of relevant information as a patient moves between care settings so that the next provider can understand recent diagnoses, treatments, medicines, allergies, tests, and plans.

concepts.name: Connectivity
concepts.definition: The ability of systems to send or receive data.

concepts.name: Summary of care
concepts.definition: A communication of essential information when a patient is referred or transferred, including current problems, medicines, allergies, procedures, laboratory information, demographic information, provider details, care goals, instructions, and required follow-up.

concepts.name: Authorized participant
concepts.definition: A person or organization permitted to participate in health information exchange for an appropriate purpose.

concepts.name: Patient identity matching
concepts.definition: The process of reliably associating exchanged information with the correct patient despite missing or inconsistent identifying information.

concepts.name: Data mapping
concepts.definition: The translation of local data into shared standards so that information can be interpreted across systems.

concepts.name: Centralized exchange
concepts.definition: An exchange model in which participant data are combined in a shared repository that participants query for available patient information.

concepts.name: Federated exchange
concepts.definition: An exchange model in which detailed data remain with the original organizations and a locator service helps identify where information exists before the requesting organization retrieves it.

concepts.name: Directed exchange
concepts.definition: An exchange pattern that sends information to a known authorized recipient, such as during a referral.

concepts.name: Query-based exchange
concepts.definition: An exchange pattern that allows an authorized user to search for information held by participating organizations.

concepts.name: Consumer-mediated exchange
concepts.definition: An exchange pattern that allows patients to obtain and transmit selected health information.

concepts.name: Opt-in consent model
concepts.definition: A consent model that requires the patient to agree before information is included or shared.

concepts.name: Opt-out consent model
concepts.definition: A consent model that includes information unless the patient chooses not to participate.

concepts.name: Privacy
concepts.definition: The protection of sensitive health information so that it is available only to authorized people for appropriate purposes.

concepts.name: Trust
concepts.definition: Confidence in the protections and governance of exchange that encourages people and organizations to participate.

concepts.name: Public-health use of exchange
concepts.definition: The use of information from multiple care settings for population patterns, prevention, quality improvement, planning, reporting, surveillance, alerts, immunization reporting, and disaster response.

concepts.name: Exchange workflow
concepts.definition: The process through which exchanged information is made available during a clinical task, located, reviewed, and incorporated into the current care process.

concepts.name: Standards and quality controls
concepts.definition: Shared structures, meanings, and checks that help turn transmitted data into usable information.

concepts.name: Healthcare standard
concepts.definition: An agreed way to represent, organize or exchange healthcare information to reduce ambiguity.

concepts.name: Vocabulary
concepts.definition: A set of words or phrases with defined meanings.

concepts.name: Clinical terminology
concepts.definition: A representation of detailed clinical concepts and their relationships for documentation and care.

concepts.name: Classification
concepts.definition: A method of grouping conditions into categories for statistics, reporting or reimbursement.

concepts.name: Code set
concepts.definition: Standardized identifiers used to store or transmit defined information.

concepts.name: Exchange standard
concepts.definition: Agreed structures for packaging and communicating messages, documents or healthcare resources.

concepts.name: ICD
concepts.definition: The International Classification of Diseases groups health conditions for reporting, statistics, reimbursement and research.

concepts.name: SNOMED CT
concepts.definition: A detailed clinical terminology of health concepts including findings, symptoms and conditions.

concepts.name: LOINC
concepts.definition: A standard for naming and identifying laboratory tests and many clinical observations.

concepts.name: RxNorm
concepts.definition: A standardized terminology for clinical drugs, including ingredients, strengths and dose forms.

concepts.name: CPT and HCPCS
concepts.definition: US procedure and service codes used for administrative reporting, claims and reimbursement.

concepts.name: HL7
concepts.definition: A family of healthcare information exchange standards, as well as the organization that maintains them.

concepts.name: FHIR
concepts.definition: An HL7 exchange standard based on reusable resources such as Patient, Observation, Medication and Encounter.

concepts.name: FHIR resource
concepts.definition: A reusable structured representation of a healthcare concept for information exchange.

concepts.name: Semantic interoperability
concepts.definition: The receiver can interpret exchanged information with the intended clinical meaning.

concepts.name: Code mapping
concepts.definition: Connecting local identifiers to shared codes, with review when meanings do not match exactly.

concepts.name: Clinical context
concepts.definition: Relevant attributes such as unit, date, method, status and patient identity needed to interpret information.

concepts.name: Implementation guide
concepts.definition: Additional rules specifying how exchange standards should be applied in a defined use case.

concepts.name: Standard version
concepts.definition: A specified release of a standard which may affect compatibility and interpretation.

concepts.name: Healthcare analytics
concepts.definition: Using data, information technology and analysis to gain insight and support healthcare decisions.

concepts.name: Primary use
concepts.definition: Using data to support direct care for an individual patient.

concepts.name: Secondary use
concepts.definition: Using data beyond the immediate encounter for research, quality improvement, public health or planning.

concepts.name: Descriptive analytics
concepts.definition: Summarizes what happened using observed data, counts, averages and charts.

concepts.name: Diagnostic analytics
concepts.definition: Examines differences and relationships that might explain an observed pattern.

concepts.name: Predictive analytics
concepts.definition: Estimates a future or unknown outcome using existing information.

concepts.name: Prescriptive analytics
concepts.definition: Considers appropriate actions in response to an observed or predicted situation.

concepts.name: Data warehouse
concepts.definition: Organizes information for reporting and analysis.

concepts.name: Data lake
concepts.definition: Stores large quantities of varied data for later processing.

concepts.name: Data dictionary
concepts.definition: Explains field names, definitions, units, valid values and collection methods.

concepts.name: Preprocessing
concepts.definition: Preparing data by cleaning, addressing missingness, checking duplicates and normalizing formats.

concepts.name: Feature engineering
concepts.definition: Selecting, transforming or combining existing data elements for analysis.

concepts.name: Supervised learning
concepts.definition: Uses examples with known outcomes to predict or classify other cases.

concepts.name: Unsupervised learning
concepts.definition: Identifies patterns or groups without a predefined outcome.

concepts.name: Reinforcement learning
concepts.definition: Learns from feedback based on actions and their outcomes.

concepts.name: Classification model
concepts.definition: Assigns a category to observations.

concepts.name: Regression model
concepts.definition: Estimates a numerical value.

concepts.name: Clustering
concepts.definition: Forms groups based on data patterns and similarity.

concepts.name: Model evaluation
concepts.definition: Checks usefulness using performance measures, calibration, fairness, usability and consequences of errors.

concepts.name: Data drift
concepts.definition: Changes over time in data or practice that may affect model usefulness.

concepts.name: Accuracy
concepts.definition: A recorded value correctly represents the patient, event, measurement or condition.

concepts.name: Completeness
concepts.definition: Required information is present for the intended use.

concepts.name: Consistency
concepts.definition: Comparable data use compatible definitions, categories, formats and units.

concepts.name: Timeliness
concepts.definition: Data are current and available when needed.

concepts.name: Natural language processing
concepts.definition: Methods that make human-language data usable by computers, while requiring care with negation, timing and uncertainty.

concepts.name: Data cleaning
concepts.definition: Checking for impossible, duplicated, inconsistent or incorrectly coded values.

concepts.name: Missing data
concepts.definition: Data that are not asked, known, applicable or entered.

concepts.name: Imputation
concepts.definition: Replacing a missing value using a defined and documented method.

concepts.name: Descriptive quality checks
concepts.definition: Counts, percentages, averages, ranges, distributions and crosstabs used to investigate data quality.

concepts.name: Data visualization
concepts.definition: A purposeful display of patterns, comparisons, trends and distributions.

concepts.name: Bar chart
concepts.definition: A chart used to compare categories or groups.

concepts.name: Line chart
concepts.definition: A chart used to show changes across time.

concepts.name: Histogram
concepts.definition: A chart used to show the distribution of a numerical variable.

concepts.name: Table
concepts.definition: An organized display of exact values, with clear headings, units, timeframe and source.

concepts.name: Exploratory data analysis
concepts.definition: Understanding the shape, patterns, relationships and plausible limits of data before formal analysis.

concepts.name: Dashboard
concepts.definition: A collection of selected measures to support monitoring and action.

concepts.name: Five rights of clinical decision support
concepts.definition: The right information, person, format, channel and time.

concepts.name: Big data
concepts.definition: Data often described by high volume, velocity and variety.
